newsitem.title: FRANCE: French grain expert dismisses U.S. subsidy threat.
newsitem.headline: French grain expert dismisses U.S. subsidy threat.

text.p: A senior French farm official called America's bluff over grain subsidies on Wednesday, saying its threat to respond to EU export aid by subsidising its own grain exports was a hollow one.
"I think if they had much merchandise this year they would already have done it," Michel Marie, president of French cereals office ONIC, told a news conference on grain supplies.
U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman warned this week that Washington could not watch the European Union subsidise exports indefinitely without restoring its own aid scheme.
But European officials have said the prospect of U.S. subidies seems remote given that it had an unusually tight harvest last year and most of that is already sold out.
Subsidies are used to bridge the gap between European grain prices and the lower prices affordable to importers.

Another ONIC official, director general Alain Moulinier, said both Europe and the United States sides were allowed to use grain export subsidies up to certain limits under the Uruguay Round global trade pact signed in 1994.
Whether or not Washington chose to take advantage of this was a matter for the United States, he said.
Privately, however, several EU officials are worried about stirring up past tensions over subsidies and Brussels has told Washington it will try not to undercut American farmers.

Glickman on Monday urged the U.S. Congress to back President Bill Clinton's FY-1998 budget request for $500 million for the Export Enhancement Program (EEP), the U.S. grain subsidy scheme which has been on ice since July 1995.
U.S. officials say there are no immediate plans to bring back EEP subsidies but they will look at this again if EU subsidies start to hurt U.S. grain sales.
